progressions.name: Axis of Awesome
progressions.description: The most common pop progression, used in hundreds of hit songs. Named after the comedy group that famously medleyed dozens of songs using this progression.
songs: No Woman No Cry - Bob Marley

progressions.name: 50s Doo-Wop
progressions.description: The classic doo-wop progression from the 1950s. Creates a nostalgic, romantic feel that defined an era of music.
songs: Stand By Me - Ben E. King
Every Breath You Take - The Police

progressions.name: Sensitive Female
progressions.description: Starting on the minor vi chord gives this progression a more emotional, introspective quality. Popular in contemporary pop and indie music.

progressions.name: Andalusian Cadence
progressions.description: A descending progression with Spanish/Flamenco roots. Creates dramatic tension that resolves powerfully. Common in rock, metal, and Latin music.
songs: Hit the Road Jack - Ray Charles
California Dreamin - The Mamas and the Papas

progressions.name: 12-Bar Blues
progressions.description: The foundation of blues, rock and roll, and countless other genres. The dominant 7th chords give it that classic bluesy sound. This 12-bar structure has been the backbone of popular music for over a century.
songs: Pride and Joy - Stevie Ray Vaughan
The Thrill Is Gone - B.B. King

progressions.name: Jazz Turnaround
progressions.description: The most important progression in jazz. The ii7-V7-Imaj7 creates smooth voice leading with rich 7th chord voicings and is the building block of jazz harmony.
songs: Fly Me to the Moon - Frank Sinatra

progressions.name: Pachelbel's Canon
progressions.description: Based on the famous Baroque composition. This progression has been borrowed by countless pop songs for its elegant, flowing quality.
songs: Don't Look Back in Anger - Oasis

progressions.name: Minor Blues
progressions.description: A darker take on the blues progression. Common in minor key songs across rock, R&B, and soul music.
songs: The House of the Rising Sun - The Animals

progressions.name: Classic Rock
progressions.description: The simplest and most powerful progression. Just three chords that built rock and roll and countless folk songs.

progressions.name: Creep Progression
progressions.description: Named after the Radiohead song. The surprise major III and the minor iv (borrowed from parallel minor) create an unsettling, emotional quality.

progressions.name: Pop-Punk
progressions.description: An extended version of the Axis progression with an added iii chord. Common in punk and pop-punk music.
songs: Sugar We're Goin Down - Fall Out Boy

progressions.name: Royal Road
progressions.description: Popular in Japanese pop and anime music. Creates a sense of forward momentum and emotional resolution.

progressions.name: Reggae
progressions.description: A laid-back progression common in reggae, ska, and salsa. The return to IV before repeating creates a relaxed, cyclical feel.

progressions.name: Minor Descending
progressions.description: A minor progression that descends then ascends. Creates a moody, contemplative atmosphere popular in modern pop and R&B.
songs: Babe I'm Gonna Leave You - Led Zeppelin
Writing's on the Wall - Sam Smith
My Heart Will Go On - Celine Dion

progressions.name: Flamenco Minor
progressions.description: A simple minor progression with the major VI chord adding brightness. Common in Latin, flamenco-influenced, and minor key pop songs.
